title: SG-8 Suggest What Happens Next contribution modal
summary: Accessible Radix modal opened from gameplay for submitting and viewing contributions via the Go backend client
description: Context: ContributionSheet is a plain div dialog with a bare textarea, a Send button and a best-effort own-suggestions list, opened from a button in App. Desired behavior: a Radix modal opens from the gameplay screen without navigation, with a prompt textarea, remaining count, submit button with disabled and loading states, inline success and error feedback, validation (empty, over-length, quota exhausted) and a history list, using only the existing client in game/frontend/src/api/client.ts. Expected result: players contribute without leaving the game, with keyboard and focus handled correctly. Why: the StoryForge redesign requires a polished in-game contribution UX with no Firebase, no database and no Git credentials in the browser.
acceptance_criteria: Given the gameplay screen, when the Suggest What Happens Next button is activated, then a modal dialog opens without any navigation or URL change
Given an open modal, when the player submits valid text, then the existing submitContribution client call is used and success or error feedback appears inline
Given empty text, over-length text or an exhausted quota, when the player tries to submit, then no API call is made and an inline validation message is shown
Given an open modal, when it opens, closes or Escape is pressed, then focus moves into the dialog, is trapped, and returns to the trigger on close

in_scope: App wiring of the trigger button
out_of_scope: Firebase, database or Git credentials in the browser
preserve: submitContribution and listMine contracts in client.ts

technical_constraints: React + TypeScript, Radix Dialog (@radix-ui/react-dialog already in package.json)
Use only the existing client in src/api/client.ts for submit and history
definition_of_done: All requirements delivered and their Verify units green
